data.name: Neriyah
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Neriyah means 'my light, my brightness'. This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'ner', which means 'light', and is a feminine variant of the masculine name Neriah. In the Bible, there are several characters with this name, including a Levite priest and a wife of King Hezekiah.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the light and brightness of God, and the illumination of the soul.
data.numerology_meaning: A harmonious, balanced, and loving name. Those with the name Neriyah tend to be nurturing, caring, and creative individuals.

in_hebrew.name: נְרִיָּה
in_hebrew.meaning: אור דולק, איש אור, אור נעלם, לאור יוצא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נְרִיָּה הוא שם אשר נושא בתוכו אור של תורה, הוא שם הנושא את האור הנצחי, המאיר שבעת היום, ואור העולם, הבא לבריאה, ה' עבדך, נְרִיָּה, תפארת עמי, תמיד יהי' צדק ותמימות.

in_greek.name: Νεριά
in_greek.long_meaning: Νεριά είναι όνομα που συνδέεται με το φως, την απαγγελία της αλήθειας, και τον δρόμο της σωτηρίας. Εμφανίζεται στη Βίβλο ως έπitheton ουσιαστικό που περιγράφει το προσωπείο του Θεού, την απόκτηση της σοφίας, και την ανάδειξη της αλήθειας.

in_latin.name: Neriah
in_latin.long_meaning: Neriah est nomen quod significat lux, luxuria, splendor. In Scriptura Sacra, Neriah est nomen quod praedicat Christum, qui est lux aeterna, lux mundi, et lux vitae.

in_english.name: Neriyah
in_english.meaning: light, shining one, radiant, luminous, shining light
in_english.long_meaning: Neriyah is a name that conveys light, truth, and salvation. Derived from Hebrew roots, it signifies the radiance of God's presence, the illumination of wisdom, and the revelation of truth. In Christian tradition, Neriyah is associated with the light of Christ, which guides us through the darkness and leads us to eternal life.

biblical_reference.note: In the Bible, Neriah is the name of a grandson of Shaphan, a scribe of King Josiah and a companion of Jeremiah.

data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Neriyah represents the divine light of God that shines within each of us, guiding us through life's challenges and bringing hope and illumination to our souls. historical_references.reference: The name Neriyah is mentioned in the Old Testament Book of Ezra, as the name of a priest who returned from Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem to rebuild the Temple.
historical_references.context: The Second Temple Period, during which the Jewish people rebuilt the Second Temple in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament book of Luke, the name Neriah is mentioned as the name of a high priest during the time of King Herod the Great.
historical_references.context: The period of the Herodian Dynasty, during which Herod the Great expanded the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem and ruled the region as a client state of Rome.
